title: ebay | How To | Ship a small item on eBay
description: As a new seller on eBay, you may find there are many different options when it comes to shipping. This video is intended to help simplify the shipping processes and ensure that you can get the item to your buyer quickly and easily. To get the co-branded eBay & USPS boxes shipped to you for free, go to http://ebay.to/2j7HfvZ. eBay YouTube Customer Support Hours are Monday – Friday, 6:00AM – 6:00PM PST. For help outside these hours, please contact eBay Customer Service at http://ebay.to/2iXYNIC

asr.full_text: Hi, my name is Autumn, I'm a customer service representative here at eBay but I'm also a seller. I've been selling for a couple of years now and I just wanted to share with you some of my best practices on shipping an item. As a new seller, shipping on eBay might seem daunting at first, but it's actually really easy. eBay gives you plenty of options to choose from. There's FedEx, we have UPS, USPS, and each of those has their own option to ship underneath. If you want to go economy, we do have an option for that. If you want to get it to them the next day, you can do that too. I like to offer free shipping for all of my items because it does put my listing higher up in search results. But eBay does offer you the option to provide a flat rate or calculated based on buyer's location, and that can be internationally or national. Once you've listed an item, it's time to package it up. One of the things I like to do is pre-package my items before it sells to cut back on my handling time. So last night I listed some Sony PlayStation controllers and how I usually package them is wrapping up the cords in a rubber band and wrapping the whole controller in bubble wrap before I put them in the box together side by side. I usually get my boxes from USPS. eBay does have a service online where they will ship boxes to your house for free. So weighing your item is one of the most important steps in shipping. You want to make sure that you are as accurate as possible so you're not surprised with any cost later on down the road. Using a scale can give you the most accurate weight, but make sure that you include the weight of the shipping items themselves, like the box and whatever you're using to fill the box up with. Once your item sells, you're going to want to print a shipping label. To do that, you go to the right-hand side of your screen, where it says My eBay, and click on Selling. Once you get there, you scroll down to your sold folder and find your item. To the right of your item it'll say print shipping label. A benefit of printing off a shipping label directly from eBay is not only is it more cost-effective, it also uploads that tracking number immediately to your account. If you take an item to the post office, you need to make sure that you grab that tracking number and put it onto the item immediately when you get home. Don't worry about needing any label paper. It will print on any computer paper you just need to cut and tape to your box. I hope you've enjoyed this video and it's relieved any stress you may have had around shipping. Just remember, if you have any questions or concerns, we are always here to help.
